questions.question: How will a player understand the fixed evolution branch and the long support route before committing to raise it?

description:
The Listening Wood’s familiar caterpillar has a pale-blue Bug/Ice form. It is an ordinary regional animal; no new supernatural origin has been established. The existing larva retains Wurmple’s ordinary moves, including Poison Sting, despite its Bug/Ice form. Its level-10 split is fixed by the individual’s personality rather than rerolled on each attempt. Glaciverm is the early fully evolved physical branch; Frostcoon is a long support commitment before Nivalora at level 55.

Proposed ecology: larvae feed along the sheltered underside of leaves and retreat toward branch joints when rain shakes the foliage. Fine silk caught across a fork and a line of clipped leaf edges give the player signs to notice before seeing the animal. A forestry encounter could let the player pass quietly or disturb the branch; this is proposed scene behavior, not an implemented interaction.

Proposed encounter detail: a patch of silk with fresh leaf clippings is occupied; a dry broken strand alone may mark an abandoned perch. After a passing Natu shakes the branch, the caterpillar waits at the fork, then reaches back toward the same leaf. A patient player can learn that movement rather than shaking every tree. Handling a recruited Wurmple means offering a stable surface to crawl onto instead of pulling against its anchor.

data.description: Level 10, the other fixed personality branch
Existing forest-grass encounters at levels 3–5; its later stages are currently reached by raising this form.
